key_insight: Discrete CNOT routing can limit both the reachable expressivity of a variational quantum circuit and the local gradient directions available for training, so routing geometry matters as much as parameterization.
engineering_relevance: This suggests quantum circuit design should jointly optimize architecture and trainability, using routing-aware insertion rules to add useful descent directions without changing the current model output.
method: Separate CNOT routing matrices from continuous one-qubit rotations to analyze capacity and local tangent accessibility.
Derive operator Schmidt-rank and multiblock bounds to quantify expressivity limits and Bell-pair fidelity obstruction.
Use routing-conditioned identity insertion and projection-based scores to rank new routing choices while preserving the current unitary.
evidence_signal: Exact-statevector experiments reported strong short-horizon score-to-loss descent correlations on Bell tasks, effective selector behavior on Heisenberg chains up to 12 qubits, and routing-dependent stagnation in a broader TFIM ensemble.
watch_item: The routing-aware gains are demonstrated on exact-statevector benchmarks, so scalability and noise robustness on larger or hardware-executed circuits remain to be validated.
paper_title: When Expressivity Is Not Enough: Discrete Routing Geometry in Variational Quantum Circuits
